_comment: Guardian Shield v9 policy. Two postures: (1) agent-containment (default, hardening_mode=false) restricts only AI-agent process subtrees against protected_paths; (2) hardening_mode=true is DEFAULT-DENY - it protects the critical_paths set against EVERYONE except TAG_TRUSTED (trusted_exes), and turns on the self-protection hooks (bpf()/module/mount/dev-mem/ptrace). protected_paths/critical_paths are directory/file prefixes (trailing slash auto-stripped). agent_exes are launcher basenames -> TAG_AGENT. exempt_exes are full exe paths -> TAG_EXEMPT (override inherited AGENT). trusted_exes are full exe paths -> TAG_TRUSTED (unrestricted, may call bpf(); MUST include the loader's own path).
_critical_comment: Enforced (against all-but-trusted) ONLY when hardening_mode=true. The shield's own state (pins + install dir) + credentials. Adjust the install-dir path to wherever the loader/bpf.o/config actually live on the target host.
_trusted_comment: MUST include the loader's own exe path or it cannot load/pin/unpin under hardening_mode. Set this to the deployed loader path. (The loader also trusts itself by exe inode, so a relative-path invocation still works.)
_supplychain_comment: SUPPLY-CHAIN / CREDENTIAL-HARVEST DEFENSE (always-on, independent of the two postures above). build_exes are launcher basenames whose exec taints the whole install subtree (TAG_TAINTED, inherited + sticky). credential_paths is the crown-jewel AssetMap: a TAINTED (build-tool) or AGENT subtree is DENIED any open (incl. read-only) of these, so a malicious npm/pip postinstall cannot read+exfil your AWS/SSH keys. A normal/trusted/untainted process reading its OWN creds is unaffected. TIERING: crown jewels only - build-tool self-secrets (~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.cargo/credentials) are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED here (tools legitimately read them during install; no build tool legitimately reads your AWS/SSH keys). Expand the /home/USER paths for the target user.
_egress_comment: EXFIL BLOCK (supply-chain, always-on for tainted/agent subtrees). A TAINTED build-tool subtree (or AGENT) may only connect() to allowlisted destinations; a connect to any other public IP (a webhook.site / attacker C2) is logged (EV_TAINTED_CONNECT) and, if enforce_egress, denied with -EPERM BEFORE the connect completes. The loader ALWAYS seeds loopback + RFC1918 private + link-local + CGNAT, so LAN/localhost/registry-mirror-on-LAN work; egress_allow adds operator public CIDRs. TRADEOFF (honest): with enforce_egress=true and only the private defaults, a tainted `npm install` reaching a PUBLIC registry (registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, crates.io, github.com) is DENIED unless you allowlist that registry's CIDRs here. This is the cost of egress-jailing build tools; set enforce_egress=false to log-only (detect) first, or add the registry CIDRs. IPv4 only in the trie; IPv6 loopback/link-local/ULA are allowed inline, global IPv6 is treated as public (no operator IPv6 allowlist in v1).
